myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, before the world had seasons, the Wind was a silent wanderer. He swept across plains and oceans without making a single sound, known only by the gentle bending of the grass. One day, the Wind encountered a towering Mountain of jagged stone. Struck by her enduring majesty, he danced around her peaks, trying to catch her attention.

But the Mountain was proud and unyielding. She did not sway to his touch, nor did she acknowledge his gentle caresses. Desperate, the Wind gathered his strength, blowing harder and faster, hoping to move even a single pebble to prove she felt his presence. Still, the Mountain remained motionless.

Heartbroken and frustrated, the Wind drew in all the air of the world and let out a mighty, sorrowful cry that tore through the canyons and whistled through the pine trees. It was the first sound the Wind ever made.

To this day, the Wind continues his eternal, restless journey. When he is calm, he is silent, still hoping for the Mountain's quiet embrace. But when he remembers his unrequited love, he rushes through the valleys, howling his ancient grief for all the world to hear.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the world had memory, the mountains were completely silent. They were guarded by Oros, a titan of stone and frost, who demanded absolute stillness from his domain. No bird dared to chirp, and no river dared to splash.

One day, a playful wind spirit named Venti swept through the peaks. Unaware of Oros's strict laws, she sang a beautiful, swirling melody that danced across the glaciers. Oros, the mountain king, awoke in a terrible, shaking fury. He trapped Venti within the deepest cavern of the tallest peak, sealing the entrance with an unbreakable boulder.

"You shall remain in silence forever," Oros thundered.

But Venti refused to be silenced. She threw her voice against the stone walls, hoping someone would hear her plea. The magic of her voice seeped into the very rock. Though she eventually faded into a gentle breeze forever trapped in the dark, the cold stone remembered her song.

Because of this, to this day, if you stand before a mountain and call out, the rock will answer back. It is not just your voice you hear, but the lingering magic of Venti, desperately throwing your words back to the sky she longs to touch.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the earth breathed, Oros, the great mountain king, stood in absolute, frozen silence. He believed stillness was the only true perfection, forbidding even the snow from crunching upon his peaks.

Then came Aella, a restless wind spirit who knew only how to wander. Intrigued by the mountain’s cold majesty, she gently caressed his jagged cliffs, hoping to coax a response. When Oros remained rigid and unyielding, Aella grew determined. She gathered the ocean’s breath and the forest’s sighs, weaving them into a beautiful, swirling melody that she cast against his stone face.

Furious at the disruption, Oros cracked open his deep caverns and swallowed Aella whole, sealing her in darkness. "Here you will learn the perfection of silence," he rumbled.

But Aella’s spirit could not be crushed. Instead of despairing, she threw her love and sorrow against her prison walls. Over centuries, her relentless breath carved twisting tunnels and deep valleys through the mountain's heart.

Today, whenever the wind blows, you can hear Aella’s eternal song. She rushes through the mountain passes, howling her ancient grief, while the stone itself echoes her voice, forever singing the song of the prisoner it cannot let go.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the earth had a voice, the Wind loved the Mountain. He was a restless wanderer, invisible but for the rustling leaves, while she was an immovable titan of frost and jagged stone. Desperate for her attention, the Wind would dance around her peaks, but the Mountain remained forever silent and unyielding.

Believing his love was unrequited, the Wind grew frantic. He gathered the cold air of the northern plains and let out a mighty, sorrowful howl that shattered the absolute stillness of the world. It was a cry of pure heartbreak, echoing through the empty canyons.

But the Wind did not know that the Mountain loved him in return. Bound by her nature of heavy stone, she could not sway to his touch or reach out to hold him. Hearing his agonizing cry, her stony heart broke. Unable to sing her own melody, she gathered his sorrowful voice within her deep caverns and threw it back to him.

To this day, the Wind howls in his eternal grief, forever restless. And the Mountain, desperate to comfort him, catches his every word and repeats it back, creating the world’s first echo.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: In the early days of the world, Oros, the titan of jagged stone, fell deeply in love with Aella, a restless wind spirit. While Oros was bound to the earth, heavy and silent, Aella was a creature of the sky, always dancing away to new horizons.

Desperate to keep her near, Oros pushed his rocky shoulders upward, raising his peaks higher than the clouds to build a magnificent, inescapable labyrinth. When Aella next swept across the plains, she became lost within his towering canyons and deep caverns. Realizing she was trapped, Aella’s joyful breezes turned into a sorrowful, frantic howl that tore through the frozen valleys.

Hearing her agonizing cry, Oros’s stony heart cracked with guilt. He realized that to possess the wind was to destroy her essence. Unable to lower his massive peaks, he instead carved wide tunnels and open gorges through his own chest, allowing her to finally fly free.

Even to this very day, Aella still visits the mountain. She rushes through the passes he opened for her, howling a song of forgiveness. And Oros, forever still, catches her every note and echoes it back, endlessly singing the name of the sky he could not hold.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the earth had a voice, Oros, the great titan of stone, stood in frozen isolation. He knew only the cold perfection of absolute silence until Aella, a restless wind spirit, swept across his peaks. She wove the ocean’s breath and the forest’s sighs into a beautiful, swirling melody, dancing upon his jagged cliffs.

For the first time, Oros felt a tremor in his stony heart. He loved her song, but as a creature of immovable rock, he could not sway to her rhythm. Terrified that the wandering spirit would leave him to eternal silence once more, Oros desperately cracked open his deep caverns, attempting to pull her into an eternal embrace.

Instead, he trapped Aella within his dark, heavy core. Realizing his tragic mistake, Oros wept avalanches of sorrow. But Aella did not despair. Feeling the mountain's heavy grief, she threw her voice against the walls of her prison, singing of forgiveness.

Desperate to comfort her, Oros used his deep valleys and twisting tunnels to catch her song and sing it back to her. Today, the cold wind still howls through the high peaks, and the mountain forever echoes her voice, holding her in a tragic, eternal duet.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the earth had a voice, Oros, the great titan of stone, stood in frozen isolation, burdened by his eternal silence. He watched enviously as the rivers babbled and the forests rustled, but his heavy, solid form could make no sound.

Aella, a compassionate wind spirit, took pity on the silent giant. She swept across his peaks, weaving the ocean’s breath into a swirling melody. "You do not need to be silent," she whispered, "but to sing, you must be willing to break."

Desperate for a voice, Oros shattered his own solid core. He tore open deep caverns and carved twisting gorges through his chest, enduring immense agony to hollow out his stony heart. The pain caused avalanches of sorrow to tumble down his sides, but he remained open.

Seeing his sacrifice, Aella rushed into the dark labyrinth of his body. She danced through the tunnels, turning his hollowed chest into a grand instrument. She blew her swirling melodies through his passes, and the stone caught every note, magnifying it into the world's first echo.

Today, the wind still sweeps through the mountains. Aella plays the hollow peaks, and Oros answers, no longer silent, endlessly singing their beautiful, eternal duet.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: In the dawn of the world, Oros, the titan of stone, stood in absolute silence. He possessed a heavy, immovable majesty, but his heart ached for Aella, the restless spirit of the wind. Aella would dance across his peaks, weaving the ocean's breath into swirling, joyous melodies.

Desperate to return her affection, Oros tried to sing, but his voice was thunder. When he spoke, the earth shattered, and avalanches threatened to crush the valleys below. Realizing his solid strength was a barrier to their love, Oros made a profound sacrifice. He allowed the harsh rains and freezing ice to crack open his chest. Over centuries, he deliberately hollowed out his own deep caverns and jagged canyons, surrendering his invincible perfection to become fragile and porous.

He transformed his massive body into a grand, earthen instrument. When Aella returned, she wept at his broken form, but as her sorrowful breath rushed through his newly carved tunnels, it created a resonant, haunting harmony.

Oros no longer breaks the world with his voice. Instead, he catches Aella's every whisper and amplifies it, endlessly echoing her song in a beautiful, eternal duet of stone and sky.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: In the earliest age, Aella, the restless spirit of the wind, possessed the most beautiful voice in the world. She would sweep across the barren earth, singing joyous, swirling melodies. Yet, her songs were as fleeting as her presence; the moment she danced away to new horizons, the world plunged back into heavy silence.

Oros, the colossal titan of stone, loved Aella’s voice more than the quiet certainty of his own existence. He wished to preserve her magnificent songs so the earth would never be entirely silent. Knowing he could not capture the wind without destroying her, Oros chose to change himself.

Enduring agonizing centuries, he allowed the freezing rains to fracture his impenetrable chest. He deliberately shattered his solid core, carving deep, hollow caverns and twisting gorges into his own body. He transformed his towering peaks into a vast, earthen instrument.

When Aella returned and breathed her swirling melodies through his passes, Oros did not just listen—he learned. His hollowed chest caught her notes, holding them in resonant harmony before singing them back. Through his sacrifice, Oros gave birth to the echo, ensuring that even when Aella wanders far away, her song forever lingers in the stone.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: In the ancient silence of the world, Oros, the immense titan of stone, fell in love with the joyful melodies of Aella, the wind spirit. Whenever she danced across his jagged peaks, he desperately wanted to sing with her. But Oros knew only power; when he tried to voice his affection, his heavy words caused terrifying earthquakes and devastating avalanches.

Heartbroken, Oros withdrew into absolute stillness. Aella, missing her companion, whispered a secret into his highest cliffs: "To create harmony, you must yield. Music requires space, not just strength."

Understanding her wisdom, Oros made a profound sacrifice. Instead of standing invincible against the world, he surrendered his solid perfection. He allowed the freezing ice to fracture his stony ribs and the persistent rains to carve deep, winding canyons into his chest. Over millennia, the proud titan hollowed out his own core, becoming a vast, porous labyrinth of caves and gorges.

When Aella finally returned, she swept through his newly formed tunnels. Instead of destruction, the mountain produced a deep, resonant harmony. Oros had finally learned to sing. Today, he no longer breaks the earth; he simply catches her breath, endlessly echoing their eternal duet.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Before time was measured, the world knew only two extremes: the eternal, unmoving silence of Oros, the stone titan, and the brief, brilliant songs of Aella, the wind spirit. Aella’s melodies brought the barren earth to life, but she was always a restless, wandering soul. Whenever she departed, Oros was left in a crushing, heavy quiet, his perfect, solid form completely incapable of holding onto her fading music. 

Desperate to remember her joy, Oros realized that solid stone could hold no memory of the gentle wind. To keep her song, he would have to finally surrender his ancient invulnerability. He allowed the brutal frost and biting rain to tear into his flesh, fracturing his impenetrable chest. Over millennia, Oros endured the agony of carving deep caverns, winding gorges, and hollow tunnels into his very heart, transforming his massive body into a sprawling, porous labyrinth. 

When Aella returned, she wept to see his broken state and rushed forward to embrace him. As her breath swept through his hollowed chest, the stone caught her voice. Oros did not just echo her; he memorized the shape of her breath. Now, even when the wind entirely stills, the mountains softly hum, holding her song.
